generations.name: First generation
generations.note: The first car officially called S-Class. ABS arrived here in 1978, a world first, and the 6.9 was a 6.8-litre hot rod in a banker suit.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.note: The over-engineered era at full strength. Bruno Sacco styling, million-mile durability reputations, and the definitive 1980s boardroom car.

generations.name: Seventh generation
generations.note: A screen-led cabin and mild-hybrid sixes and eights. The S580's V8 is the traditionalist pick before electrification takes the class over.

models.intro: The car the rest of the industry copies five years later. Air suspension, massaging seats, night vision, if it debuts anywhere, it debuts here. The name is short for Sonderklasse: special class. It has earned it more often than not.

generations.name: First generation (pre-name lineage)
generations.note: Built like a vault and styled like one too. The Porsche-built 500 E hid a 5.0 V8 in this shell and quietly outran sports cars.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.note: The four-headlight face matured, quality recovered from the cost-cutting years, and the E55/E63 AMG versions were genuine muscle cars.

generations.name: Fifth generation
generations.note: A mini S-Class in tech and cabin, including the wagon the US actually got in All-Terrain form. The E450's six is the sweet spot.

models.intro: The taxi in Stuttgart, the boardroom car everywhere else. The E-Class line, the W124 carried it before the name existed, is Mercedes at its most durable and least theatrical, which is exactly the point.

models.collectorNote: A 300SL Gullwing is a seven-figure car in any condition that runs. Alloy-bodied cars and documented race history move the number from there.

generations.name: 300SL
generations.note: Direct fuel injection, a tubular spaceframe so tall it forced the gullwing doors, and Le Mans and Mille Miglia wins behind it. Coupe first, roadster from 1957.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.note: An 18-year production run selling one idea: a heavy, safe, V8 roadster for American boulevards. The 560SL was the flagship of the final years.

generations.name: AMG SL
generations.note: Back to a fabric roof, standard all-wheel drive, and full AMG development. The SL 63 is a GT car first and a roadster second.

models.intro: It starts with the 300SL Gullwing, the fastest production car of its day and still the collector benchmark, and continues as seven decades of open-top grand touring. The current car is an AMG product; the early car is automotive royalty.

models.collectorNote: Early W460 work trucks and the limited-run V12 G65 sit at opposite ends of the same market. Originality matters more than shine on the early cars.

generations.name: First generation
generations.note: Built in Austria by Steyr-Daimler-Puch as a working vehicle for armies and farmers. Spartan, slow, and nearly unkillable.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.note: The G goes luxury: leather and wood inside, same box outside. The supercharged G55 AMG turned the joke into a straight-line weapon.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.note: Wider, lighter, independent front suspension, and it still looks like 1979 and locks all three diffs. The G63 outsells everything else in the range.

models.intro: A military utility vehicle that became a luxury icon without changing its silhouette. Three locking differentials, a ladder frame, and door hinges on the outside, the shape is the substance, and Mercedes has wisely never messed with it.

generations.name: First generation
generations.note: Dry-sump V8 mounted behind the front axle. The GT R added rear steering and active aero and took the fight directly to the 911.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.note: Bigger, heavier, all-wheel drive, and 2+2 seating, a GT in the true sense now. The GT 63's pace is not in question; the character changed.

models.intro: AMG's own car, not a tuned Mercedes: a front-mid V8, a transaxle at the back, and a long bonnet with the cabin sitting nearly over the rear wheels. The second generation shares its bones with the SL and got more civilised; the first one is the purist's pick.
